parameters.query:
-- The whole batch in one statement. A loop would let one bad item abort the
-- rest, and the point of this endpoint is that it cannot.
--
-- Every item the caller sent gets an answer, including duplicates, so the
-- response lines up with the request rather than silently being shorter.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT a.ord, x.*
      FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS a(elem, ord),
           LATERAL jsonb_to_record(a.elem) AS x(
               source_id       int,
               url             text,
               title           text,
               publisher       text,
               published_at    timestamptz,
               excerpt         text,
               raw_text        text,
               source_language text,
               section         text
           )
),
-- Postgres refuses to touch the same row twice in one statement, so the same
-- URL sent twice has to be caught here rather than by ON CONFLICT.
numbered AS (
    SELECT i.*, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY i.url ORDER BY i.ord) AS seen
      FROM input i
),
checked AS (
    SELECT n.*,
           CASE
             WHEN n.url IS NULL OR btrim(n.url) = ''
               THEN 'url is required'
             WHEN n.title IS NULL OR btrim(n.title) = ''
               THEN 'title is required'
             WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sources s
                               WHERE s.id = n.source_id AND s.active)
               THEN 'unknown or inactive source_id'
             WHEN n.seen > 1
               THEN 'duplicate of an earlier item in this batch'
           END AS reject_reason
      FROM numbered n
),
stored AS (
    INSERT INTO items (source_id, source_url, canonical_url, title, publisher,
                       published_at, excerpt, raw_text, source_language,
                       section, status, fetched_at)
    SELECT c.source_id, c.url, c.url, c.title, c.publisher, c.published_at,
           c.excerpt, c.raw_text,
           -- fall back to whatever language the source publishes in
           coalesce(c.source_language,
                    (SELECT s.language FROM sources s WHERE s.id = c.source_id)),
           c.section, 'new', now()
      FROM checked c
     WHERE c.reject_reason IS NULL
    ON CONFLICT (canonical_url) DO UPDATE
       SET title        = EXCLUDED.title,
           publisher    = EXCLUDED.publisher,
           excerpt      = EXCLUDED.excerpt,
           raw_text     = EXCLUDED.raw_text,
           published_at = EXCLUDED.published_at,
           fetched_at   = now()
    RETURNING id, canonical_url
)
SELECT c.ord,
       c.url,
       c.reject_reason IS NULL AS accepted,
       c.reject_reason         AS reason,
       s.id                    AS item_id
  FROM checked c
  LEFT JOIN stored s
         ON s.canonical_url = c.url AND c.reject_reason IS NULL
 ORDER BY c.ord;
